assets.prompt:
Use case: productivity-visual
Asset type: 16:9 website service hero for SEO / AI Answers
Primary request: Create a premium photorealistic operations scene that clearly shows one believable SEO and AI-answer workflow: a real customer question becomes structured website content, then appears as an organic search result and as a cited AI answer.
Scene/backdrop: sophisticated real research-and-content workstation in a dark editorial studio; physical keyboard, mouse, notebook and a large calibrated monitor on the right. The monitor shows a practical shippable interface with four visibly connected stages: question research, structured page/content editor, organic search result, and cited AI answer. Use restrained connector lines within the screen UI only.
Style/medium: premium commercial photography blended seamlessly with realistic product UI; credible agency workstation, not concept art.
Composition/framing: wide landscape, 16:9. Reserve the left 38-42% as dark copy-safe negative space with no important objects or labels. Concentrate detailed workflow on the right 58-62%. Slightly elevated three-quarter camera, 35mm editorial lens, realistic screen perspective.
Lighting/mood: low-key cinematic studio light, warm off-white screen surfaces, near-black environment, controlled reflections, subtle restrained crimson highlights.
Color palette: near-black #111111, warm off-white #F5F0E8, restrained #C91C1D only for active states and connecting details.
Materials/textures: matte black metal, warm paper grain, real glass reflections, subtle fabric and desk wear.
Text (verbatim): "QUESTION", "CONTENT", "SEARCH", "AI ANSWER", "CITED". Render these exact short labels only, clean and legible; no other visible words.
Constraints: the workflow must be understandable at a glance and technically believable; organic search result is not an ad; cited AI answer visibly references the structured content; shippable modern UI, natural proportions, premium website quality; no logos, no brand names, no watermark.
Avoid: gibberish, fake paragraphs, abstract machinery, gears, floating holograms, sci-fi, neon cyberpunk, generic dashboards, excessive red, duplicated screens, decorative charts unrelated to the workflow.

Use case: productivity-visual
Asset type: 16:9 website service hero for Social Media
Primary request: Create a premium photorealistic social-content production scene that clearly shows one real workflow from capture to edit to content calendar to short-form/feed publishing across phone and desktop.
Scene/backdrop: high-end but believable small creative studio workstation on the right, with a compact camera or phone rig, tasteful human hands trimming a real vertical video at a desktop editing station, a practical weekly content calendar, and a phone showing a finished short-form/feed preview ready to publish.
Style/medium: premium commercial editorial photography with seamless realistic shippable UI; human, tactile, operational, not abstract.
Composition/framing: wide 16:9 landscape. Keep the left 38-42% deep near-black and copy-safe with no important objects or labels. Build a clear right-side progression from physical capture device to edit timeline to calendar to phone/desktop publishing preview. Slightly overhead three-quarter view, natural hand anatomy, realistic device scale.
Lighting/mood: sophisticated warm studio lighting, controlled contrast, subtle practical red indicator lights, energetic but calm and expensive.
Color palette: near-black #111111, warm off-white #F5F0E8, restrained #C91C1D for selected timeline clips, calendar markers and publish state.
Materials/textures: matte camera body, brushed black desk, realistic skin and fabric, glass screens, paper notes with no writing.
Text (verbatim): "CAPTURE", "EDIT", "SCHEDULE", "PUBLISH". Render these exact short labels only, clean and legible; no other visible words.
Constraints: clearly different from advertising or CRM; the viewer should understand a professional ongoing social-content system; screen interfaces must be practical and shippable; no logos, no platform trademarks, no watermark.
Avoid: gibberish, fake captions, influencer glamour shot, selfie pose, multiple redundant phones, abstract machinery, gears, holograms, sci-fi, neon cyberpunk, excessive red, impossible hands, duplicated UI.

Use case: productivity-visual
Asset type: 16:9 website service hero for Digital Advertising
Primary request: Create a premium photorealistic campaign-operations scene showing a realistic paid-ad testing system: creative variants, audience and budget test controls, a matching landing page, and clear performance measurement. This is campaign optimization, not lead routing.
Scene/backdrop: dark professional media-buying workstation on the right with two realistic monitors and a physical control surface or keyboard. One monitor shows three distinct ad creative variants alongside audience segments and an A/B budget allocation control; the other shows the corresponding landing-page preview and a restrained measurement panel with conversion trend and cost indicators.
Style/medium: premium commercial photography blended with shippable product UI, credible agency campaign room, precise and modern.
Composition/framing: wide 16:9 landscape. Leave the left 38-42% near-black and copy-safe with no important objects or labels. Arrange the operational detail on the right in a clear visual sequence: creative test -> audience/budget decision -> landing page -> measurement. Eye-level three-quarter camera, realistic screen perspective and human-scale controls.
Lighting/mood: focused low-key studio light, crisp warm screen glow, disciplined analytical mood, subtle crimson active states.
Color palette: near-black #111111, warm off-white #F5F0E8, restrained #C91C1D for selected creative, budget split and key measurement only.
Materials/textures: matte workstation surfaces, real monitor glass, brushed metal, subtle fingerprints and desk wear.
Text (verbatim): "CREATIVE", "AUDIENCE", "BUDGET", "LANDING PAGE", "MEASURE". Render these exact short labels only, clean and legible; no other visible words.
Constraints: creative variants must visibly differ; audience and budget controls must look usable; landing page must visually correspond to the selected ad; measurement must be clear but not a generic wall of charts; no CRM, inbox, contact cards, routing arrows, logos, brand names or watermark.
Avoid: gibberish, fake ad copy, abstract machinery, gears, floating holograms, sci-fi, neon cyberpunk, stock-market trading screen, excessive red, duplicated dashboards, lead-routing flowcharts.

Use case: productivity-visual
Asset type: 16:9 website service hero for Customer Nurture
Primary request: Create a premium photorealistic lifecycle-operations scene that clearly shows one practical customer-nurture system: a real inquiry enters, is segmented, receives an email/SMS/reminder sequence, and results in an appointment or a reactivated customer.
Scene/backdrop: believable service-business lifecycle workstation on the right with a laptop, phone and small appointment calendar display. The main practical interface shows a horizontal or gently stepped customer timeline with one inquiry card, segmentation choice, email message, SMS message, reminder, then two clear end states: booked appointment and reactivated customer.
Style/medium: premium commercial editorial photography seamlessly combined with shippable lifecycle UI; warm, human and operational, not a conceptual infographic.
Composition/framing: wide 16:9 landscape. Preserve the left 38-42% as clean near-black copy-safe negative space with no important objects or labels. Concentrate the complete lifecycle timeline and real devices on the right 58-62%. Slightly elevated natural camera angle, realistic proportions, no floating interface detached from devices.
Lighting/mood: warm controlled studio light suggesting thoughtful follow-through and trust, deep shadows, soft off-white interface, restrained crimson progress markers.
Color palette: near-black #111111, warm off-white #F5F0E8, restrained #C91C1D for active sequence steps, appointment confirmation and reactivation state.
Materials/textures: matte black desk, real phone glass, warm paper/calendar texture, subtle everyday wear.
Text (verbatim): "INQUIRY", "SEGMENT", "EMAIL", "SMS", "REMINDER", "APPOINTMENT", "REACTIVATE". Render these exact short labels only, clean and legible; no other visible words.
Constraints: make the sequence immediately understandable and realistic for a service business; email and SMS are distinct; appointment and reactivation are clear outcomes; practical shippable UI; no logos, no brand names, no watermark.
Avoid: gibberish, fake paragraphs, sales pipeline stages, ad creative variants, abstract machinery, gears, floating holograms, sci-fi, neon cyberpunk, excessive red, duplicated messages, impossible devices.
